evidence: Cic. Tusc. 4.19.43: nisi īrā excanduit fortitūdō (Lewis & Short)
Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.12.2: id postquam rescīvit, excanduit (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase; ferveō, to boil, is used of passions. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: Lewis & Short: excandesco · Lewis & Short: ferveo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 98.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
